text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Stocks climbed to a record high as Friday's surge on Wall Street rippled over the Atlantic, boosting investor confidence. The FTSE 100 rose 6.7 points to 4,031.5, but off its earlier high during the session of 4,046.8.
FRANKFURT- German shares also ended at a record. The DAX index of 30 blue chip stocks rose 19.36 points to 2702.64. In after-hours trading the index stood at 2,705.21.
PARIS - French shares edged lower after Wall Street prices retreated Monday, having spent the day in a narrow trading range. The blue-chip CAC-40 index fell 1.14 points to 2,151.55.
ZURICH - Swiss shares shrugged off morning doldrums and also rose. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed up 8.08 points at 2,439.99.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended mixed after moving in narrow ranges and languishing at weaker levels for most of the day, shrugging off Friday's surge on Wall Street. The key 225-share Nikkei 225 average closed up 12.98 points at 21,161.01.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks staged a powerful rally, with the Hang Seng index registering its biggest point gain since March, as new records on Wall Street and strong interest in China shares kept buyers active. The Hang Seng rose 227.56 points to 12,133.07.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market, inspired by record highs on Wall Street, closed within striking distance of the record high of 2,350.1 set on Feb. 3, 1994. The All Ordinaries index closed up 24.3 points at 2,339.8, near its highest level this year.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares got a late shot in the arm from a strong Wall Street. The overall index rose 15.7 points to 7,036.3 as the industrials jumped 23.3 points to 8,245.7. The gold index fell 5.9 points to 1,727.9 on concern over weakening price for the metal.
